Denver housing at a glance

Colorado's capital sits in the South Platte valley on the plains side of the Front Range. Census takers found 715,522 people in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 740,613. Denver is also a county, merged since 1902, which means a single government handles assessing, taxing and recording. A seller usually needs fewer phone calls than elsewhere in Colorado.

Renters outnumber owners. Only 48.8% of homes are owner-occupied across 335,428 households (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied value is $616,000 and median gross rent is $1,831. A good share of sales involve a landlord, an heir or an investor who wants out. The median covers the entire city. A particular house can price well away from it, depending on condition, neighborhood and lot.

Hail and your roof

For Denver roofs, hail is the weather problem that costs the most. Among American cities with 50,000 or more people, Denver ranks 10th for hail proneness, and three of the ten costliest hailstorms on record in the country struck here. Snowfall averages 53.5 inches a year, July highs average 89.9 degrees, and the record of 105 degrees was set June 28, 2018.

A beaten-up roof, split siding or a claim that never led to repairs can stall a mortgage-financed sale, because the lender and the inspector both study roofs. Be ready for these questions:

  • Did anyone file a claim for the hail damage, and was the work done, or was it left?
  • How old is the roof, and will a new owner's insurer cover it?
  • Have sun and freeze-thaw cycles marked the stucco, deck or paint?

Paperwork helps. Someone paying cash may also accept the damage as part of the deal.

Taxes in Denver come due after the year they cover, and the Treasury Division collects them.

Weekend and holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. Statements live online. Look up your address in the property search tool, open Tax Documents and download the year you need. Taxes at closing

On closing day the current year's tax gets divided by the closing agent, one share for you and one for the buyer. Treasury also issues a Certificate of Taxes Due for Real Property, which the title company uses to learn what a parcel owes. Any earlier year still open must be paid for the transfer to be clean. On appeals and assessment timing, the Denver Treasury property tax page is the place to start.

The state fee on a Denver deed

When a deed transfers property for more than $500, Colorado adds a documentary fee of $0.01 per $100, as county recording pages explain. Denver files deeds through the same county system. Look for that fee, the recording charge and any transfer forms on your settlement statement. Choosing a cash buyer leaves these items alone, but it can shorten the wait between signing and recording because no lender has to release loan funds.

Short-term rental rules

In Denver, a short-term rental needs a license and has to be the host's own primary residence. The business license number goes in each ad, and violators risk fines or losing the license.

That bites if you own a second Denver property that was running as an Airbnb. With the primary-residence rule, a house its owner does not live in cannot lawfully operate as a short-term rental. Such a house may have to be sold or leased long term, and a buyer who was counting on nightly income may offer less. Read the city's rental, zoning and licensing pages for your address before you list or take an offer.

Landlords, heirs and life changes

Jobs in government, hospitals, schools and aviation keep demand strong near downtown. They offer no protection against a layoff, a divorce or an inherited house nobody wants to run. Events like those, more than the market, push Denver owners toward quick sales.

Inherited a house? Collect the documents showing who has authority to sign, and ask the title company what it needs before it books a closing. Own a rental with a tenant in place? Learn early whether a buyer will take it occupied. Cash buyers often do.

Deciding what to fix first

Before spending a dollar, price out the one repair a buyer will notice from the street. In Denver that is usually the roof. If a claim was paid and the work never done, expect a buyer's insurer to ask about it, and expect the number on any offer to reflect that. If the claim was settled and the roof replaced, keep the receipts and permit records in one folder.

Cosmetic work rarely pays back on a house that is being sold quickly. Clean it out, mow, and let the buyer decide what they would change. The goal is a clear picture of what the house needs, so the offers you receive are comparable.

Paperwork to gather

Pull four items together: the latest tax statement from the property search tool, any loan payoff details, your lease and rent roll if a tenant lives there, and any city rental license if the house ran as a short-term rental. Having them ready means the title company can start its search the same day you accept an offer, and nobody has to wait on a missing page.

Three ways to sell a Denver house

Owners usually pick between an agent listing, a sale on their own and a cash purchase, and each swaps price for time and effort.

  • Agent listing: often the best price for a house in good shape, though you wait through showings, repair requests after the inspection and the buyer's loan approval.
  • Sale on your own: the commission stays in your pocket, and the pricing, disclosures and forms become your job.
  • Cash sale: the buyer accepts the house in its current state, which means no repair list and, often, a closing day of your choosing.

Cash fits deferred maintenance, hail damage, a tenant in place or an estate that must be settled. A listing fits a clean house and a roomy calendar. Compare both before you decide. Our cash offer comes with no obligation.

Steps in a Denver cash sale

  1. Send the address and describe the house.
  2. We review it and return a written offer.
  3. After you accept, a title company searches the record, requests the Certificate of Taxes Due from Treasury and drafts the deed.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and the money is yours.

Set the offer beside a listing first if you like. Saying no costs nothing. Keep your tax statement close, since the property search tool lets you download it in a few minutes.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the median home worth in Denver?

Census data for 2020 to 2024 puts the middle of the owner-occupied market at $616,000. Any single house can sit far from that figure, so read it as a citywide benchmark.

When are Denver property taxes due?

You can pay half by the last day of February and half by June 15, or pay everything by April 30. Weekend and holiday deadlines roll forward a business day.

Can I sell a Denver house that was used as a short-term rental?

Yes. Denver requires both a license and a host who lives there, so a house missing either may draw questions from a buyer. A cash buyer can take it as it stands, but settle any city fines or unpaid taxes.

Does hail damage stop me from selling a house in Denver?

No. Hail is so common here that buyers expect it. A damaged roof can pull the price down or complicate financing, so plenty of owners with roof damage look at an as-is sale.

What is the state documentary fee in Colorado?

One cent for every $100 of consideration on a deed above $500. County recording pages describe it that way, and you will see it listed at closing.

Colorado Springs housing at a glance

Pikes Peak rises behind Colorado Springs, the El Paso County seat, roughly 70 miles down the highway from Denver. Only Denver has more people in Colorado. Plenty of local sellers are working against a clock, usually a military assignment or a new job.

The military and the local market

Service members and their families account for much of the demand. About 45,000 active-duty troops lived in the area as of 2021, and defense work, military and contractor together, supplies more than 40% of the Pikes Peak region's economy. The big installations are Fort Carson, the Air Force Academy, Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases and Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station.

When one sector carries that much weight, a decision at a base or a large employer can shift buyer interest quickly. If you have orders with a report date, build the sale around that date rather than around the market.

Property tax calendar

Taxes on Colorado Springs property are billed and collected by El Paso County. A year goes in this order.

Real estate taxes still unpaid are advertised in September, then offered at a public auction in October. From September 30 on, the Treasurer will accept only cash or certified funds. When a deadline lands on a weekend or legal holiday, it slides to the next business day.

Climate, hail and wildfire

Expect a dry, sunny place: about 243 sunny days a year, 16.5 inches of precipitation and 38 inches of snow in a normal season. March is the snowiest month and the July to August monsoon brings most of the rain. The city logs 18 days a year at 90 degrees or hotter and 5.2 nights below zero, and lightning strikes are frequent. All of that is rough on roofs, gutters, decks and paint.

Fire has left a mark. The Waldo Canyon blaze began on June 23, 2012, about 4 miles northwest of the city. It destroyed 347 homes inside the city limits and sent 32,000 residents out, and the Black Forest fire a year later did more damage. Ask your insurer how it treats wildfire at your address, and expect buyers in wooded neighborhoods to raise the subject too.

Short-term rental permits

Renting a home for 29 days or less takes a city permit at $124.95, good for one year. Renew on time, because the city offers no grace period.

An application includes proof of primary residence, a liability policy of at least $500,000 and a link to the listing on your hosting platform. Two units on a property need two permits. Staff has 10 business days to review a complete application.   • An agent listing can earn a higher price on a house in good shape. The trade is time spent on showings and the buyer's financing.
  • Selling it yourself keeps the agent's fee, though disclosures and paperwork land on you.
  • A cash purchase is as is. Repairs, wear and doubts about hail or fire-season insurance will not hold up the closing.

Selling while on military orders

A buyer relying on a loan adds risk when your assignment date is fixed, because a delay in underwriting can run past your report date. A cash buyer takes that risk off the table. Let the title company know early that you will be away, ask which signing arrangements it accepts, and hand over your tax statement and any payoff details before you go. Most of the rest can be completed without you in the room.

What happens at the closing table

After you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens, confirms the tax position with the Treasurer and prepares the deed and closing statement. You sign, the deed is recorded, and the proceeds go to you once debts on the property are paid. With no lender involved, nobody is waiting on an appraisal or a loan committee, so the date is mostly a matter of when the paperwork is clean and when you want to be done.

If a lien or a back-tax balance turns up, the closing statement shows it and the payoff comes out of your funds. Ask to see a draft statement a day or two ahead so you can question any line.

  • your most recent tax statement from El Paso County
  • payoff information for any mortgage or lien
  • the short-term rental permit and its renewal dates, if the house was rented
  • insurance claim records for hail or fire damage

If anything is missing, say so at the start. The title company can usually find it, and nothing here has to be perfect before you ask for an offer.

The first half falls on the last day of February, the full-year option on April 30 and the second half on June 15. Taxes unpaid after the second-half date become delinquent.

Yes, for stays of 29 days or less. The permit costs $124.95, lasts one year and requires proof of primary residence and $500,000 in liability insurance.

It can. The 2012 Waldo Canyon fire destroyed 347 homes in the city, so buyers and insurers in wooded areas ask about fire risk. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands.

Yes. A cash sale avoids waiting on a buyer's loan, which helps when an assignment date is fixed. Ask the title company early what signing arrangements it accepts if you are away.

Boulder at a glance

Flood risk and flood insurance

Boulder calls itself the number one flash flood risk community in Colorado, and anyone buying a house in a mapped floodplain will have to sort out insurance.

  • Flood coverage on most policies does not start for 30 days, so a buyer who shops late may close without it.
  • Since the city joined the Community Rating System in 1992 and reached a Class 5 rating in early 2013, standard policyholders get a 25% discount.

Pull up the city's interactive floodplain map and find your lot before you list or accept an offer. If a certificate exists, give the title company a copy so the buyer's insurer gets it fast.

Rain began around September 9, 2013, and the flooding was worst on September 11 and 12. Several spots in the city recorded 15 to 20 inches between September 9 and 15. Boulder County averages about 20.7 inches in a whole year, meaning five days delivered a full year of rain.

On September 12 Boulder Creek ran above 5,000 cubic feet per second. Its normal flow is 150 to 200. In the county, 262 homes were destroyed and nearly 300 more were damaged, and three deaths were confirmed. A major disaster was declared for the county.

If the license cannot continue, the house is worth what it is as a regular home or long-term rental, and a buyer who plans the same use will adjust the offer accordingly.

An investor who buys for cash can look at those facts quickly, without waiting on a lender's rules about rental income, and decide on the spot.

Ask the El Paso County Treasurer for a payoff figure at (719) 520-7900, and have your title company order a Certificate of Taxes Due. Old unpaid balances can end up in the tax lien sale.

Can I sell my Fountain house if it needs repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to finish repairs first. The offer reflects the condition of the house.
